claim: BlackRock tells investors growth will come from API calls, without naming the product behind them
earlier_receipt: https://s24.q4cdn.com/856567660/files/doc_presentations/2025/BLK-Investor-Day-2025-WEB.pdf (downloaded fresh, 147 pages), slide 23: "4. Continuously drive marginal costs down / All of BlackRock is built on a foundation of operating excellence in everything we do and what we do will continue to rapidly grow" ... "2030 Estimate ... Metric / Increase by 2030 ... BlackRock: Portfolios (#) 2x, Model Portfolios (#) 4x; BlackRock + Aladdin®: Trade Allocations (#) 1.3x, API Calls (#) 17x" ... "Our objective is for the marginal cost of this growth to be as low as possible through continued investment in scale enablement". A grep of the whole deck for API/Studio/developer/interoperab finds only "API Calls (#)" on slide 23. A second-source web search (for an Investor Day transcript) could not run because the WebSearch budget was used up.
earlier_finding: The words "growth will come from API calls" are wrong. The slide lists API calls as one of four operating volumes expected to grow, the fastest at 17x, under a marginal-cost theme. It does not say that revenue or business growth comes from API calls. "Without naming the product" is correct, because Studio is not mentioned anywhere in the deck. Suggested wording: "BlackRock tells investors API calls will grow faster than any other volume it measures (17x by 2030), without naming the product behind them." The same fix applies to doc_layout.txt:496, "BlackRock itself says growth will come from API calls".

claim: Both [Data Cloud and Explore] are Studio surfaces
earlier_receipt: Source 16 page: "where the data cloud and Aladdin data cloud specifically comes in, which is part of Studio". https://www.blackrock.com/aladdin/platforms/products/aladdin-studio: "Aladdin Data Cloud (ADC) is a managed data-as-a-service offering that brings together Aladdin—the language of portfolios—with Snowflake's data platform". The Studio page never mentions Explore. /home/user/ai_game/blackrock-aladdin/04-transcripts/part2-cloudfront-and-podcasts/047_An_introduction_to_Aladdin_Climate.md:42 (Whisper of the introduction-to-aladdin-climate webinar): "Explore is our standard application to understand aggregated analysis for investment and risk management"
earlier_finding: The wrong word is 'Both'. Data Cloud is part of Studio (16, 14). Explore is a standard Aladdin application and no source calls it a Studio surface. Rewrite: 'Data Cloud is part of Studio; Explore is an Aladdin app that calls the same APIs.'

claim: So Copilot’s tools are Studio’s APIs
earlier_receipt: /home/user/ai_game/blackrock-aladdin/04-transcripts/part1-youtube-and-site/16_How_BlackRock_Built_Production_AI_Agents_for_Asset_Managemen.md:20: "The first, we come to define a tool as kind of mapping one-to-one to an existing Aladdin API already out in production. Kind of the second onboarding path that we give to these development teams for very complex workflows is the ability to spin up a custom agent and also plug that into the system." ZenML (URL above): "Custom agents: For complex workflows, teams can spin up their own agents and register them in the system". Studio page: "Aladdin Studio APIs enable you to build your own solutions."
earlier_finding: Overstated in two ways. (1) Only one of the two onboarding paths maps tools to APIs; the other plugs in custom agents. (2) No source says those production APIs are the ones Studio exposes to clients. Suggested wording: 'So many of Copilot's tools are wrappers on Aladdin's production APIs, the same estate Studio opens to clients', with the second clause marked as the author's inference from [1] and [8].
